title.value: Conditionally Adaptive Multi-Task Learning: Improving Transfer Learning in NLP Using Fewer Parameters & Less Data
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the document and summarizes the focus on improving NLP transfer learning using adaptive multi-task learning with fewer parameters and less data.
title.quote: C ONDITIONALLY A DAPTIVE M ULTI -T ASK L EARNING : I MPROVING T RANSFER L EARNING IN NLP U SING F EWER P ARAMETERS & L ESS D ATA

analysis.description: This paper presents a novel Transformer based Adapter called Conditionally Adaptive Multi-Task Learning (CA-MTL) aimed at improving transfer learning in Natural Language Processing (NLP). The approach integrates a new conditional attention mechanism and task-conditioned modules to foster weight sharing and memory retention. The paper discusses methodologies for more efficient knowledge transfer using fewer parameters and less data, showing competitive results on multiple NLP tasks.

type.justification: The research focuses on empirical validation of a novel training methodology for NLP tasks, providing experimental results and comparisons with state-of-the-art models.
type.quote: Through this construction, we achieve more efficient parameter sharing and mitigate forgetting by keeping half of the weights of a pretrained model fixed. We also use a new multi-task data sampling strategy to mitigate the negative effects of data imbalance across tasks.

name.justification: The paper discusses improvements on NLP tasks and benchmarks like GLUE, indicating that the primary research field is Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Multi-Task Learning (MTL) networks have emerged as a promising method for transferring learned knowledge across different tasks. However, MTL must deal with challenges such as: overfitting to low resource tasks, catastrophic forgetting, and negative task transfer, or learning interference. Often, in Natural Language Processing (NLP), a separate model per task is needed to obtain the best performance.

name.justification: The research contributes primarily to the enhancement of transfer learning techniques within NLP.
name.quote: Using Conditionally Adaptive Learning, we seek to improve pretraining knowledge retention and multi-task inductive knowledge transfer.

name.justification: The paper proposes a novel approach to Multi-Task Learning (MTL), aiming to improve parameter efficiency and performance.
name.quote: Multi-Task Learning (MTL) networks have emerged as a promising method for transferring learned knowledge across different tasks.

is_contributed.justification: CA-MTL is the main contribution of the paper, introducing a new multi-task learning approach.
is_contributed.quote: We propose a novel Transformer based Adapter consisting of a new conditional attention mechanism as well as a set of task-conditioned modules that facilitate weight sharing.

is_executed.justification: The paper includes experiments and evaluations of CA-MTL, indicating the model has been executed.
is_executed.quote: We show the efficacy of CA-MTL by: (a) testing on 26 different tasks and (b) presenting state-of-the-art results on a number of test sets as well as superior performance against both single-task and MTL baselines.

is_compared.justification: CA-MTL is compared with other models in terms of performance across various NLP tasks.
is_compared.quote: Compared to other BERT Large methods on GLUE, our 8-task model surpasses other Adapter methods by 2.8% and our 24-task model outperforms by 0.7-1.0% models that use MTL and single task fine-tuning.
